title: Don't just slap on a chatbot: building AI that works before you ask
talk_summary: A product designer argues against bolting chat interfaces onto tools, showing an issue tracker where AI proactively watches user input and suggests contextual questions, sub-issue splits, and timeline/resource actions inline. The three stated rules are: supplement user agency, recommend rather than force, and stay inside the natural workflow with one-click revert.

takeaways.what_they_do: AI watches the issue being written in real time and, without being asked, proposes the clarifying questions and a sub-issue breakdown based on prior similar issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our AI didn't wait for user input it saw someone reporting a legality share and immediately started asking the right questions

takeaways.what_they_do: AI actions are surfaced as reversible proposals inside the existing workflow rather than autonomous edits, keeping the human in control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can revert the changes easily with one click you're still in charge

takeaways.what_they_do: They identify friction points where users stop to ask for help and patterns in repeated questions as the target list for proactive automation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: identify patterns in your users's behavior where do they usually need help what questions do they always ask

takeaways.technique: Inject prior-art context at the point of action
takeaways.what_they_do: The suggestion engine uses previous data on how similar work was organized, not just the current text, to propose structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI has all the previous data knows how it was done before
